title: Passage and Compass
premise: Zephyrine Hartwell has spent years piloting the riverboat Kestrel alone, staying ahead of debts, grief, and the law that wants her brother's name. When a dying prospector named Elias Vane trades her a map to a silver vein for one promise—carry his daughter's letter over the mountains before the snows close the pass—Zephyrine discovers the map is also evidence: proof that the mining company murdered Elias's partner and framed her brother for it. Pursued by company enforcers who want both map and messenger buried, she joins forces with Odile Marchand, a surveyor with her own reasons to hate the company, and the two fall in love even as duty pulls them apart—Odile sworn to testify, Zephyrine sworn never to stop moving. In the climax at the pass, they outrun the first blizzard, deliver the letter, and choose each other over escape: Zephyrine surrenders the map to the territorial court, trading her invisibility for her brother's freedom, knowing survival now means standing still long enough to be seen.
about_author: Juniper Sandoval is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons on inland waterways before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction blends hard-won knowledge of remote landscapes with a deep fascination for people who can't afford to be found.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Running cargo upriver, she finds prospector Elias Vane dying on her deck and accepts his bargain: safe passage in exchange for a sealed letter and a folded map he refuses to explain. When company men board at Coyle's Landing asking after 'a woman captain,' Zephyrine realizes the map marks more than silver—it names her brother. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve; she stops running from the past and starts running toward it.

chapters.title: What the Surveyor Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Zephyrine and Odile Marchand, a disgraced company surveyor who recognizes the map as her own stolen work—the evidence of the mine collapse the company covered up. Forced together on the overland trail, they spar, trade truths, and begin to trust. Enforcers burn a waystation behind them, making retreat impossible. Emotional beat: wary alliance kindling into something tender neither will name yet, while loyalty to old promises strains against new ones.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Odile's POV dominates. Above the tree line, the enforcers ambush them at a frozen creek; Zephyrine takes a bullet keeping the map dry, and Odile must choose between saving her or the satchel holding the letter and evidence. She saves Zephyrine—and confesses she once signed the report that buried the truth. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; love confessed in the open cold, where hiding is no longer possible for either of them.

chapters.title: Where the River Ends
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They reach the pass town as the blizzard hits, deliver Elias's letter to his daughter, and face the choice: flee across the border together, or stay and testify. Zephyrine hands the map to the magistrate, choosing her brother's name over her own safety; Odile stands beside her as witness. The trial looms, but so does spring. Emotional beat: resolution through surrender—not defeat, but the discovery that stopping, once unthinkable, is where home begins.
